headline: WHEAT DROPS 3.4%; WASDE SETUP TAKES SHAPE
subheadline: Black Sea peace talk headlines hit wheat hard; soybean oil gives back Thursday's gains as diesel cracks keep crude firm into Labor Day.
lead: Wheat had its biggest single-session drop in weeks, off 25 cents to $7.16, as Black Sea peace talk headlines pulled the geopolitical floor out from under a market that had been leaning on export disruption as a price prop. December corn eased to $5.37, beans slipped to $13.10, and the complex went into Labor Day weekend in risk-off mode with Thursday's export sales already digested.
the_takeaway: Wheat lost its war premium today; the September WASDE on the 11th writes the next chapter.
teaser: Wheat dropped 25 cents on peace talk headlines. The rest of the complex followed. Thursday's export number is in the books.

one_number.unit: US beef export value gain, July year-over-year
one_number.context: July beef exports rose 6% in value despite China technical barriers still blocking volume. That demand signal matters for cattle pricing into fall; it is the offset to the import-proclamation headline that has been dragging live cattle.

yesterdays_call.summary: Called corn down toward $4.99. December corn settled $5.37 today, off 3.5 cents but nowhere near the $4.99 line.
yesterdays_call.note: Miss, plain and simple. The call's level was never in range.

sections.title: WHEAT DROPS ON PEACE TALKS
sections.body:
- Chicago wheat fell 25 cents to **$7.16**, its biggest single-session decline in weeks, after headlines about Black Sea peace talks hit a market that was pricing in persistent export disruption from the Russia-Ukraine conflict, ongoing since February 2022.
- The geopolitical premium that had been propping the $7.20-$7.40 range came out fast; funds were long and had no reason to stay once the headline crossed.
- India's weak monsoon and lower grain production, flagged this week, were not enough to offset the peace-talk headline; the export-disruption story was carrying too much weight.
sections.catalyst: Black Sea peace talk headlines removed geopolitical export-disruption premium from wheat.
sections.bottom_line: Wheat needs to hold $7.16 through the long weekend or the next leg tests $6.90.
sections.vs_yesterday: Wheat: Wednesday's drop extended; now a two-day 35-cent slide.

sections.title: GRAINS EASE INTO LABOR DAY
sections.body:
- December corn settled at **$5.37**, off 3.5 cents, in a quiet drift lower with no fresh catalyst beyond the broader grain complex softness following wheat's break.
- November beans gave back 5 cents to $13.10; soybean oil dropped 3.3% to $68.74, erasing recent gains as the crush-margin story rotated back toward meal, which barely moved at $345.30.
- CPKC reporting a record start to the crop year says export logistics are not the bottleneck; the question heading into the September WASDE is yield, not pipeline.
sections.catalyst: Soybean oil fell 3.3% as crush-margin balance shifted; CPKC record crop-year start signals logistics are clear.
sections.bottom_line: Corn at $5.37 is consolidating; the September WASDE on the 11th is the next real directional input.
sections.vs_yesterday: Beans: held better than corn again; meal/oil split continued its rotation.

sections.title: CATTLE HOLD; BEEF EXPORTS FIRM
sections.body:
- Live cattle settled at **$213.15**, off half a percent, holding a narrow range; the Cargill multi-plant lockout, ongoing since May 19 and still removing roughly 6,000 head of daily processing capacity, keeps packer margins the binding constraint rather than cattle supply.
- July beef export value rising 6% year-over-year is the demand signal the board needed; Rep. Figures introducing the Protecting American Beef Producers Act to reverse the Trump beef import order adds political noise without changing today's math.
- Feeders at $325.20 held within half a percent as the Aug 24 Douglas, AZ phased port reopening for Mexican feeder imports continues to price into the spread.
sections.catalyst: July beef export value up 6% year-over-year; Protecting American Beef Producers Act introduced in House.
sections.bottom_line: Cattle acting like the buyer is patient, not gone; the import bill is a watch item, not a market mover yet.

sections.title: DIESEL CRACKS KEEP CRUDE FIRM
sections.body:
- WTI crude settled at **$91.37**, off less than a percent, as diesel tightness and elevated crack spreads kept a floor under crude even as the broader risk-off tone dragged equities.
- The EIA flagged elevated crack spreads as the main driver of pump prices; Rosneft's CEO put China, not OPEC, at the center of oil market stability, which fits the pattern of the Iran-Hormuz cycle, a July re-escalation that has since cooled with the premium deflating into August.
- For fall fieldwork, diesel input costs are the operative number, not crude.
sections.catalyst: Record diesel crack spreads per EIA; Rosneft CEO credits China buying for market stability.
sections.bottom_line: Crude holding $91 on diesel demand; the fall fieldwork cost story is diesel-specific, not crude-broad.

outside_the_pit.title: China Rare Earth Firms Freezing US Exports Before Xi-Trump Summit
outside_the_pit.body: Chinese rare earth producers with valid export licenses have stopped shipping to the US ahead of the Xi-Trump summit, fearing government repercussions. Rare earths touch precision agriculture equipment, electric motors in grain handling, and the supply chain for anything with a circuit board on the farm.

outside_the_pit.title: Ag Economy Barometer: Farmers Hold Farmland for Family, Not Just Returns
outside_the_pit.body: August 2026 Purdue Ag Economy Barometer results show farmland ownership is driven heavily by family and sentimental factors, not current financial returns. That behavior caps forced-sale pressure in down years and tells lenders something different than raw land-value models show.

weekly_thread.question: Will today's Crop Progress rating confirm the August yield cuts or add a weather premium back into corn and beans?
weekly_thread.status_text: Crop Progress showed no dramatic weather deviation to reprice the USDA August yield cuts; the September WASDE at 11:00 AM CT on the 11th is now the authoritative next answer.

the_more_you_know.title: WASDE WHEAT HISTORY SAYS BIG FRIDAY DROPS OFTEN STICK
the_more_you_know.body: In the four WASDE cycles since 2022 where wheat fell more than 20 cents on the Friday before the report, three of the four settled lower still on WASDE day. The geopolitical-premium unwind tends to front-run the number, not reverse it.

watch_list.desc: Labor Day: CME grain and livestock markets closed. No USDA releases.
Weekly export sales: wheat under 250K MT extends the peace-talk demand doubt; beans above 700K MT resets the board.
September WASDE: corn yield above 181.5 bu/acre pressures December below $5.30; below 179.5 reopens the premium.
Douglas, AZ feeder cattle port reopening: feeder/live spread narrowing below $110 signals returning Mexican supply is pricing through.

daily_quote.text: Sell down to the sleeping point.
